rich_summary: Arjuna reaches a mysterious lake while searching for water and hears an unseen voice warning that he must answer questions before drinking. Ignoring the command, he drinks and falls dead instantly. Bhima follows, finds his brothers, but also drinks without answering the warning and likewise dies. When Yudhishthira arrives, he discovers all four brothers lying lifeless and mourns them deeply, reflecting on their strength and destiny. Suspecting a supernatural cause, he prepares to investigate. The Yaksha finally reveals itself and challenges Yudhishthira with a long series of philosophical questions about duty, knowledge, virtue, and human nature. Unlike his brothers, Yudhishthira responds calmly and wisely, demonstrating restraint, humility, and profound moral insight—qualities that make this famous “Yaksha Prashna” episode a central teaching moment in the Mahabharata about wisdom over impulsive strength.

top_scenes.scene_text: Yudhishthira stands beside a crystal lake in a silent forest, staring in shock at the bodies of Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva lying motionless among fallen weapons and lotus flowers.
A towering, radiant Yaksha with blazing eyes and a massive body appears perched on a tree above the lake, confronting Yudhishthira in the wilderness.
Bhima, parched with thirst, kneels at the enchanted lake ignoring the unseen warning voice as the still water reflects the surrounding forest.
